_about: Words for the slice's staged scenes, Writer's placeholder pass (VS-31, 2026-10-09; final text at VS-37, Ross approves). The scenes themselves (triggers, flags, steps) are in slice/story_scenes.json: hideout_wake, mox_deck, gate_pass, kasp_wreck, ending_gate, ending_square, ending_home. Red is silent: she only gestures, or the narrator describes her. Vela has no body in the slice, so her lines show in the plain box. The ending's small payoff follows the Level Designer's recommended option (B with a dash of A: the screens go dark, the posters come down, Pop hands over a free bowl) plus the wolf wave of option C as one narrator beat; Ross picks, and a pick is a data edit.

mk_hideout_wake.speaker: vela
mk_hideout_wake.text: Good evening, Red. Logging you as awake.

mk_hideout_wake.speaker: vela
mk_hideout_wake.text: Dispatch has a job, and the Signals are tightening the screws. Tap the deck first, so I can file where you are.

mk_rp_deck.speaker: mox
mk_rp_deck.text: {face:boasting}Red! Perfect timing! The deck is done! Mostly! Forty percent! The IMPORTANT forty!

mk_rp_deck.speaker: mox
mk_rp_deck.text: Don't say it. I know what you're thinking. 'Mox, you're a genius.' You're welcome!

mk_rp_deck.speaker: mox
mk_rp_deck.text: {face:sheepish}...Okay, maybe not. But you will. Look: four hacks. I labelled them.

mk_rp_deck.speaker: mox
mk_rp_deck.text: Zap Drone: pew. EMP: bzzzt. Overclock: you borrow someone else's gun. Reboot: you turn yourself off and on again. It heals. Do not ask.

mk_rp_deck.speaker: mox
mk_rp_deck.text: Sword hits charge the battery. So: hit things, hack things, hit things. Easy!

mk_rp_deck.speaker: mox
mk_rp_deck.text: {face:panicking}...Is it supposed to smoke? Tuesday, is it supposed to SMOKE? AAAAA!

mk_rp_deck.speaker: mox
mk_rp_deck.text: {face:focused}...Okay. Four seconds. Done. It is fine. That is how it sounds.

mk_rp_deck.speaker: narrator
mk_rp_deck.text: Mox clips the deck onto Red's wrist. It is warm. It hums. It is a little bit crooked.

mk_gate_pass.speaker: narrator
mk_gate_pass.text: Red holds up the Courier Pass.

mk_gate_pass.speaker: crowd_gate_grunt_a
mk_gate_pass.text: ...Yard 9. Huh. Nobody has gone to Yard 9 on purpose in years.

mk_gate_pass.speaker: crowd_gate_grunt_b
mk_gate_pass.text: Stamp it, then. I will find the ink.

mk_gate_pass.speaker: crowd_gate_grunt_a
mk_gate_pass.text: Stamp, stamp. In triplicate. ...Fine, once. I am out of copies.

mk_gate_pass.speaker: crowd_gate_grunt_b
mk_gate_pass.text: Keep it down on the road, courier. The Sergeant is in a mood. He has been in a mood for eleven years.

mk_gate_pass.speaker: narrator
mk_gate_pass.text: The boom barrier rattles up. Past it, the road runs off toward the ore line and a yard full of other people's things.

kasp_wreck.speaker: narrator
kasp_wreck.text: Smoke. Scrap. Somewhere in the wreck, a cupholder is still in one piece.

kasp_wreck.speaker: kasp
kasp_wreck.text: Eleven years. Eleven years, and it ends on a pile, by a courier.

kasp_wreck.speaker: kasp
kasp_wreck.text: {face:smug}This will go in my report. Under 'weather'.

kasp_wreck.speaker: narrator
kasp_wreck.text: He tucks the clipboard under one arm and limps off into the smoke, filing as he goes.

mk_end_gate.speaker: crowd_gate_grunt_a
mk_end_gate.text: Courier. Papers? ...Never mind. I saw the walker from the booth. The big one.

mk_end_gate.speaker: crowd_gate_grunt_b
mk_end_gate.text: The Sergeant will want the paperwork on this.

mk_end_gate.speaker: crowd_gate_grunt_a
mk_end_gate.text: He is going to need a bigger form.

mk_end_gate.speaker: crowd_gate_grunt_b
mk_end_gate.text: Noise ticket, one wind chime, Form 12. ...Void. I lost the pen.

mk_end_gate.speaker: narrator
mk_end_gate.text: Behind them, a wind chime tinkles in the evidence line. Nobody ducks.

mk_end_sq_intro.speaker: narrator
mk_end_sq_intro.text: Tarp Square was loud already. Now it is LOUDER. The screens go dark, the posters come down, and somebody finds the volume knob on the boombox.

mk_end_sq_intro.speaker: crowd_pop
mk_end_sq_intro.text: RED! There she is! BOWL'S ON THE HOUSE!

mk_end_sq_intro.speaker: narrator
mk_end_sq_intro.text: A bowl lands in Red's hands. It is hot. It is enormous. Her ears go straight up.

mk_end_sq_odds.speaker: crowd_odds_man
mk_end_sq_odds.text: I bet against you. Three rations.

mk_end_sq_odds.speaker: crowd_odds_man
mk_end_sq_odds.text: ...I am a terrible bettor and a wonderful loser. Here.

mk_end_sq_odds.speaker: narrator
mk_end_sq_odds.text: He presses a handful of credits into Red's hand. He looks furious about it.

mk_end_sq_legend.speaker: crowd_shopper_c
mk_end_sq_legend.text: Did you SEE it? Red beat a HUNDRED Signals wolves! With ONE ARM!

mk_end_sq_legend.speaker: narrator
mk_end_sq_legend.text: Red holds up three fingers. Then two more. Then, after some thought, a flex.

mk_end_sq_legend.speaker: crowd_shopper_c
mk_end_sq_legend.text: Three! ...Three and two more! Five hundred, with a flex! Somebody write it down!

mk_end_sq_wolves.speaker: narrator
mk_end_sq_wolves.text: The patrol comes through on the hour. The square goes quiet, from habit. Nobody ducks. One of the wolves lifts a hand, then pretends to scratch his ear.

mk_end_sq_wolves.speaker: narrator
mk_end_sq_wolves.text: The music is back before he finishes.

mk_end_home.speaker: vela
mk_end_home.text: Entry for the record. Yard 9: concluded. Sergeant Kasp: pending.

mk_end_home.speaker: vela
mk_end_home.text: You nodded just now. I am logging that as 'You are welcome.' ...And as 'Thank you.' Both.

mk_end_home.speaker: mox
mk_end_home.text: {face:proud}RED! Welcome home! I made noodles! I... bought noodles! I stood NEAR noodles!

mk_end_home.speaker: narrator
mk_end_home.text: Red taps the deck twice with a knuckle. Then she gives the neon sky a big thumbs-up, like somebody out there can see it.

mk_end_home.speaker: vela
mk_end_home.text: Goodnight, Red. Logging you as home.
